nodes.name: Build owner summary
nodes.notes: Why Code: writes the owner's order summary from an en/es message table with locale-aware amounts

parameters.content:
## Log and notify
Builds one flat row from the normalized order, upserts it into the Orders sheet keyed by order number so a retried call updates the same row instead of duplicating it, then emails the owner a plain-text summary in config.team_locale.

nodes.name: Select low-stock variants
nodes.notes: Why Code: parses the GraphQL response, de-duplicates variants, fails loudly on API errors, and words the alert in the team locale

parameters.content:
## Stock check
Reads the ordered variants' current stock and brew method from Shopify, flags any that fell below the configured threshold, and emails the owner one alert per order, in config.team_locale. No per-request timeout on this node (NOTE below); the GraphQL node retries throttling instead of failing outright, since Shopify returns throttling as a 200 response with an errors array rather than an HTTP error.

NOTE: the GraphQL node has no per-request timeout option, so a hung Shopify response blocks this execution until n8n's own default times it out. Ceiling: a slow but responding Shopify API is not bounded here. Upgrade path: switch to the HTTP Request node with options.timeout plus an explicit errors check, trading the GraphQL node's built-in NodeApiError-on-errors behavior for a manual one.

nodes.name: Build guide email
nodes.notes: Why Code: picks one guide per brew method and renders escaped HTML in the customer's language

parameters.content:
## Brewing guide (after the wait)
Waits the configured number of minutes, then reads the mounted brewing guides, picks one guide per distinct brew method among the order's known variants, and emails the customer an HTML guide listing what they bought and how to brew it, in the order's customer locale (config.default_locale when it has none). Sends nothing when the order has no email address or no line matches a known brew method.

NOTE: a wait shorter than 65 s (MAX_IN_PROCESS_WAIT_MS) stays in n8n's process memory and is lost on a restart, instead of persisting for the leader's WaitTracker to resume. That's why guide_delay_minutes must be at least 2.
